Shari Eunice T. San Pablo has advised four theses in this repository between 2024 and 2025. Their research interests and supervision patterns cover a diverse range of sub-topics, including arts and creative practice, information systems, cybersecurity and privacy, environment and sustainability, journalism and news media, mental health and well-being, educational technology, social media, and communication studies. Based on the repository data, they have supervised work involving iterative design, user interface, multimedia, narrative, and gamification.

In 2025, San Pablo advised three theses. One project, by Christian Paul R. Velo, focused on the intersection of journalism and news media, mental health and well-being, and arts and creative practice through a technical report on building a personal knowledge base for meaning-making in Obsidian. Another 2025 thesis, by Kayce Racelle G. Tampinco, explored arts and creative practice and information systems through a multimedia capsule project involving a video game about the challenges of starting new endeavors. A third 2025 thesis, by Daniel D. Dimaano, investigated educational technology by exploring the gamification of the Pomodoro Strategy and the Eisenhower Matrix to assist the learning productivity of UPOU students. San Pablo also advised a thesis in 2025 regarding information systems and cybersecurity and privacy, titled "Deceptive by Design," which utilized an interactive website to explore and simulate dark patterns in user interfaces.

In addition to thesis supervision, San Pablo has two articles in this repository from 2022. One article, titled "Fixing Information Disorder in Social Media," addresses social media, communication studies, and environment and sustainability by examining how social media platforms facilitate information disorder and disinformation. The second 2022 article, "Re(Constructing Aging): An Online Exhibit on the Filipinos Meanings of Aging," covers environment and sustainability and cybersecurity and privacy by investigating how Filipinos construct meanings of aging to inform the design of environments for older populations.

The breadth of San Pablo's supervision suggests they can support students working at the intersection of technology and social phenomena. Their supervision has included technical reports, capstone projects, and studies on user experience and productivity. While they have no advisees listed for 2026, their recent work shows a consistent engagement with how digital tools, such as personal knowledge management systems and gamified strategies, interact with human psychology and social structures. Their research profile indicates a capacity to guide projects involving multimedia, interactive design, and the social implications of digital information systems.

Shari Eunice T. San Pablo has contributed items to this repository spanning from 2022 to 2026. Their own published articles in this repository focus on several intersecting areas, including social media, communication studies, environment and sustainability, cybersecurity and privacy, and aging. Specifically, their 2022 work "Fixing Information Disorder in Social Media" addresses information disorder and media disinformation within social media platforms in relation to sustainable development goals. Their other 2022 article, "Re(Constructing Aging): An Online Exhibit on the Filipinos Meanings of Aging," explores how Filipinos construct meanings regarding aging to assist in designing environments for older populations. Based on these items, their research interests appear to involve the intersection of digital communication, social media dynamics, and social sustainability.

Their supervision shows a strength in guiding research that utilizes digital tools, such as interactive websites, video games, and personal knowledge management systems, to address psychological, educational, or social issues.
